assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 250,000 req/s peak, 80/18 read/write with 1.5% multi-partition scans and 0.5% snapshot/restore traffic.

assumptions.subject: replication
assumptions.statement: Replication factor 3. A put is modelled as one leader write plus TWO follower writes (replica visit_prob 2.0), which is why the follower tier carries more load than the leaders. A scan touches ~4 partitions (visit_prob 4.0).

assumptions.subject: consensus
assumptions.statement: This engine CANNOT model a quorum round: there is no notion of waiting for W acknowledgements, of leader election, or of read-repair. What is modelled is the WORK each replication round generates — the fan-out — and the per-hop latency. The reported latency is therefore a floor: a real quorum write waits on the SLOWEST of the two followers, not their mean.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: 75% row-cache hit rate on gets (replica visit_prob 0.25). Cache is 3 nodes at ~100k ops/s; losing the cache tier puts 200k rps straight onto the replicas, which are sized for 208k — that is the cold-cache scenario worth running.

assumptions.subject: sharding
assumptions.statement: 8 leader shards at ~8k writes/s each. The engine treats a shard set as ONE pooled component, so it assumes a PERFECTLY EVEN key distribution. A hot key or a hot partition — the most common real failure of a KV store — is invisible in this model.

_library.summary: Partitioned, replicated key-value store with a coordinator tier, row cache, and replication-factor-3 fan-out on writes.
